title: Inventory Count Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: Set the inventory count inspection scope, test readiness and requirement-level evidence, contain deficiencies, authorize status, and preserve qualified closeout.
description: An original, fillable inventory count inspection checklist form for controlling controlled physical inventory count and reconciliation package through inspection checklist identity, observations, evidence, decision, exceptions, escalation, completion, handoff, and final verification without replacing applicable requirements or professional review.
use_case: Use when a inventory control coordinator or qualified inspector must evaluate controlled physical inventory count and reconciliation package against the count plan, item master, location record, and transaction cutoff and provide a traceable basis for release, restriction, hold, correction, or rejection.

sections.title: Inventory Count inspection checklist identity and routing
sections.guidance: Anchor the record to the exact work, parties, locations, and source references.

sections.title: Inventory Count inspection scope, criteria, and readiness
sections.guidance: Define the exact population and review basis so inspection conclusions remain bounded.

fields.label: Controlled Physical Inventory Count And Reconciliation Package
Count Plan, Item Master, Location Record, And Transaction Cutoff

blocks.label: Inventory Count readiness verification
items: Count scope, zone boundaries, responsible teams, and timing are frozen
Receiving, shipping, picking, production, and transfer cutoff is documented
Blind count and system-quantity visibility rules are assigned by role
Item, unit-of-measure, pack conversion, lot, and serial references are available
Open containers, mixed lots, consignment, scrap, returns, and holds are marked
Count tags, scan devices, scales, ladders, and safety access are ready
Variance thresholds, recount independence, and approval levels are defined
Completed sheets and electronic records have controlled custody
blocks.guidance: A failed readiness item must be resolved, excluded with rationale, or carried into the exception section.

sections.title: Inventory Count requirement-level inspection results
sections.guidance: Record actual observations against explicit criteria and identify the evidence for each result.

blocks.label: Inventory Count detailed inspection points
items: Count zone and physical boundaries match the assigned sheet
Location label, SKU, description, and unit of measure are unambiguous
Sealed cases, open packs, eaches, weight, or volume are converted consistently
Lot, serial, expiry, revision, ownership, and status are captured where required
Receiving, shipping, transfer, and work-in-process cutoff is respected
Damaged, quarantined, consigned, customer-owned, or obsolete stock is separated
First count is independent and corrections remain traceable
Recount uses the specified independence and evidence rule
Empty locations and unlisted stock are explicitly recorded
Unresolved identity, ownership, cutoff, or quantity issue is escalated before posting
blocks.guidance: Checkboxes indicate that the point was examined; the result table carries findings and evidence.

sections.title: Inventory Count measurements and evidence package
sections.guidance: Preserve readings, instruments, identity, and evidence needed to reproduce the inspection decision.

blocks.label: Measurement, count, or verification log
blocks.guidance: Use the method applicable to System, first-count, recount, and approved quantity and Countability, status, ownership, and segregation condition.

blocks.label: Available inspection evidence
items: Approved count plan and zone map
Controlled count-sheet or scan-batch identity
Location and item label image
First-count and counter identity
Independent recount and verifier identity
Unit conversion or scale record
Cutoff transaction and movement log
Variance investigation and posting reference

blocks.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

fields.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

sections.title: Inventory Count exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, affected scope, immediate control, owner, deadline, and escalation reconstructable.

blocks.label: Inventory Count exception indicators
items: Unlabeled, duplicate, or inaccessible location
Unknown item, lot, serial, owner, or inventory status
Mixed unit of measure or pack conversion is uncertain
Physical movement occurred outside the documented cutoff
First count and recount remain outside the threshold
System shows stock where location is empty or the reverse
Damaged, hold, consigned, or customer-owned quantity is commingled
Count sheet or scan batch is missing, altered, or duplicated
Scale, scanner, or system interface is unavailable
Potential fraud, diversion, or deliberate record override requires escalation
blocks.guidance: Select every observed condition; do not use a generic exception mark when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Inventory Count inspection status and release decision
sections.guidance: Do not turn a checklist score into release when a critical exception or evidence gap remains.

fields.label: Inventory Accounting Or Operations Manager review

sections.title: Inventory Count inspection checklist closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: Use this inventory count inspection checklist with the applicable customer commitment, carrier terms, site policy, and retention requirements. Do not infer acceptance or release from a signature alone; unresolved identity, count, condition, custody, or proof issues require an owner, escalation, and documented disposition.

blocks.label: Prepared, reviewed, and accepted

fields.label: Reviewed by inventory accounting or operations manager

blocks.guidance: A signature records accountability for the stated decision; it does not cure missing evidence or override a stop condition.
